newsitem.title: ALBANIA: U.N. aid reaches Albanian town as soldiers watch.
newsitem.headline: U.N. aid reaches Albanian town as soldiers watch.

text.p: Ten battered trucks carrying humanitarian aid from the United Nations World Food Programme arrived in the central Albanian town of Elbasan on Tuesday after an smooth four-hour journey.

The delivery of 220 tonnes of wheat flour was watched by Italian troops, marking the first time that forces from the multinational security mission in Albania had played a role in the distribution of the humanitarian aid.
One week after the troops in the 6,000-strong force began arriving in the violence-stricken Balkan nation, the WFP convoy of 10 flatbed trucks left the western port of Durres at 8:30 a.m. (0630 GMT).

"We are here to create an environment of security along the route," said Lieutenant Colonel Simone Baschiera of the Italian armed forces in Durres before the convoy set off. "We are not going to escort them."
More than 4,000 soldiers on the eight-nation force have now reached Albania, where more than 300 people have been killed in violence after popular investment schemes collapsed.
There were hundreds of French and Italian soldiers at Durres port as the trucks prepared to leave.
A steady drizzle in the Adriatic port caused only minor delays. Workers covered the open flatbed trucks with canvas canopies before they set off.
Although the Italian soldiers said the route had been secured, there were few signs of their presence during the journey on narrow roads snaking through the hills to Elbasan.

Two jeeps with about 12 Italian soldiers carrying rifles watched as the convoy of trucks passed the town of Rrogozhine. There were more Italian soldiers and a tank further east in the town of Peqin. The food was destined for poor families in Elbasan, a worn down industrial town. About 4,430 families living below the poverty line would each be given 50-kg sacks of flour.
"It would not end my worries, but at least I would not have to worry about bread for some time," said a woman named Fatime.

"There is no malnutrition or starvation but we would like to move fast to prevent that from happening," said Laura Boldrini, spokeswoman for the World Food Programme. Relief supplies from the International Committee of the Red Cross were also transported on Tuesday, but without escorts.

Two transports carrying about three tonnes of medicines and food was dispatched from Tirana on Tuesday morning. The Red Cross has now distributed about 57 tonnes of food and 18 tonnes of medicine since early March.

"So far the Red Cross strategy of distributing small amounts on a frequent basis and accompanied by an Albanian Red Cross team has clearly proved successful," said Nina Winquist-Galbe, Red Cross spokeswoman in Tirana. "We have had no incidents."
